definitions.normative: An immutable Git commit selected from the current worktree HEAD first-parent history.
definitions.plain_language: oid and parents identify the observed commit; a failed commit attempt creates no record.

definitions.normative: A path-level change between a commit and its first parent, or the empty tree for a true root.
definitions.plain_language: Renames preserve both paths and gitlinks remain boundaries.

definitions.normative: An explicitly requested literal path set or a uniquely resolved project citation.
definitions.plain_language: Path-prefix matching is component bounded; unresolved names cannot select the first candidate.

definitions.normative: A bounded metadata projection of selected committed changes at an exact source snapshot.
definitions.plain_language: It contains no file bodies and supplies neither task intent nor session restoration.

definitions.normative: Equality of the cache source binding and current worktree, branch, HEAD, history boundary, scope, schema, and limits.
definitions.plain_language: A mismatched cache is rebuilt in memory before use; concurrent source changes mark the result stale.

definitions.normative: An explicit request to atomically persist a derived recent view inside Git-private per-worktree storage.
definitions.plain_language: Cache persistence cannot stage files, create commits, install hooks, or approve work.

open_questions: Which future task-state owner will supply goals, decisions, and unfinished work?
